statuses.label: Within County
statuses.heading: Recreational fires — no permit needed
statuses.description: Small campfires — up to 3 ft across, attended, with water on hand.
statuses.rulesMarkdown:
- 3 ft across or less, in a ring, pit, or bowl
- Clean dry firewood or charcoal only
- Someone attending the whole time
- Water on hand — 5 gallons or a charged hose
- Keep at least 3 ft of clear space around the fire, and keep it well away from structures
- Flames no higher than 3 ft
- No yard waste, garbage, plastic, or painted wood — burning garbage can draw a fine
- Burn barrels are never allowed, at any time — the Department of Ecology prohibits them
- No fires when the wind is over 10 mph
- Put it dead out before you leave it
- No permit needed, year-round, except when a burn ban is in effect
- State park, DNR, and private campground rules can differ — check the rules where you are staying
- Propane and gas appliances are tracked separately below — charcoal is not one of them

statuses.label: Propane & gas appliances
statuses.heading: Recreational fires — no permit needed
statuses.description: Self-contained propane and gas stoves, grills, and fire pits — tracked separately, so they can stay open under restrictions.
statuses.rulesMarkdown:
- Propane and gas stoves, grills, and fire pits
- No charcoal or briquettes
- Over a non-flammable surface
- 5 ft from anything that can burn
- Self-contained propane or gas appliances, where the fuel shuts off at a valve
- Charcoal, briquettes, and wood-burning BBQs are not gas appliances — they follow the recreational fire rules
- This is tracked on its own, so it can stay available when recreational fires are restricted
- Under the state burn ban, liquid-fueled and gas-fueled stoves and grills stay allowed (Proclamation 26-03)

source.says: Campfires, recreational fires, charcoal, and briquettes are AUTHORIZED.
No fires permitted at any time at Lime Kiln Point.
Fire Ban in Effect — San Juan Island National Historical Park

permits.name: Residential Burn Permit
permits.description: For piles up to 10 ft across and 6 ft tall — yard debris and brush at home. No inspection needed.
permits.rulesMarkdown:
- Piles up to 10 ft across, 6 ft tall — one at a time
- 50 ft from structures, 25 ft from property lines
- An adult attending until it is dead out
- Charged hose and shovel on site
- Clear the ground to mineral earth — dirt, gravel, or rock — at least 4 ft out in every direction
- Burn natural vegetation only. No garbage, paper, cardboard, plastics, rubber, treated wood, or petroleum
- Fire danger LOW: burn any time of day. MODERATE: 6 am to noon, out by noon. HIGH or a burn ban: no burning
- No burning when the wind is over 10 mph
- Keep the signed permit on site — it is not valid without it
- Runs through Jun 5, 2027. Burning is not allowed in an Urban Growth Area
- If the fire escapes you are responsible for suppression costs and damage (RCW 52.12)

permits.name: Commercial Burn Permit
permits.description: For piles larger than 10 ft across or 6 ft tall — land clearing and bigger burns. The district inspects the site before you light.
permits.rulesMarkdown:
- Site inspection required before you light
- Piles up to 40 ft across — one at a time
- 100 ft from structures, 50 ft from property lines
- Excavator, shovel, and water on site
- Required on site with an operator: a charged hose or water truck, an excavator, and a shovel
- Without that equipment: two full 5-gallon buckets and a shovel, and piles are capped at 5 ft across
- Clear the ground to mineral earth — dirt, gravel, or rock — at least 4 ft out in every direction
- Burn natural vegetation only. No garbage, plastics, treated wood, petroleum, or hazardous material
- Fire danger LOW: burn any time of day. MODERATE: 6 am to noon, out by noon. HIGH or a burn ban: no burning
- No burning when the wind is over 10 mph
- An adult must attend the fire until it is dead out
- Keep the signed permit on site — it is not valid without it
- No commercial burning after Jun 1, 2027, and none in an Urban Growth Area
- If the fire escapes you are responsible for suppression costs and damage (RCW 52.12)
